title: Software Estimation Is Hard. Do It Anyway. - Jacob Kaplan-Moss
summary: Jacob Kaplan-Moss: estimation is hard and overruns are common, but business needs dates, and estimating is a learnable, career-defining skill.

assertions.quote: One study by HBR found that one in six IT projects had cost overruns of over 200% and were late by almost 70%.
If you get in the habit of breaking projects down and making timeline estimates, you can review those estimates against reality and recalibrate.

verdicts.note: Jorgensen's reviews find feedback and decomposition improve estimates modestly, but overconfidence persists even in experts.

Independent studies of the Personal Software Process, which records estimates and analyses deviations from actuals, found no improvement in estimation accuracy, and a feedback-and-lessons-learned programme likewise produced none versus untrained controls.

The only software study found outcome feedback (estimate vs actual) did not improve accuracy, consistent with other domains, though it does improve assessment of estimate uncertainty; task-relation feedback is needed for accuracy gains.

assertions.quote: to go much farther than that you'll likely need to learn this skill
there are many situations where an estimate is required

verdicts.note: Reasonable synthesis; practitioner consensus rather than measured.

The authors call the NoEstimates suggestion to stop giving time predictions before a project starts 'unrealistic' while endorsing progress extrapolation, consistent with business still needing up-front estimates; effects on planning conversations are not evaluated.
